audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers print the chart as Akshan / Skill / Fiora / Fiora / Akshan / Fiora / Fiora. The packet reads Skill / Akshan / Akshan / Skill / Fiora / Fiora / Fiora, and the packet matches the prose at every disputed row: whys[0] says 'neither side owns it cleanly yet' (Skill, not Akshan), whys[2] says 'he keeps the edge' (Akshan, not Fiora), whys[3] calls it 'a genuine coin-flip' (Skill, not Fiora), and whys[4] says Grand Challenge wins any all-in (Fiora, not Akshan).
audit.why: Four of seven rows were printing a side that its own explanation contradicts. The packet and the written reasons agree; only the side arrays were wrong.
audit.corrected: Both win[] and phases[].side rewritten to Skill / Akshan / Akshan / Skill / Fiora / Fiora / Fiora with ratings 5,4,4,5,7,6,6, and phases[0..3].why rewritten so each reason states its new side.

audit.why: Spike placement is right: Akshan's level 2-3 poke window, Fiora's level 6 Grand Challenge takeover, her first-item Hydra window, and his late-game map threat via the Going Rogue revive and Comeuppance. The content layer already has all four spikes populated.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer names no cooldowns at all, dosFull/dontsFull bodies do not match their own titles, report[5].t contains the meaningless token 'Riposte his KA', and the single most important interaction is absent: Grand Challenge reveals Akshan, so Going Rogue's camouflage does not get him out of your ult.
audit.why: Heroic Swing is 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s and must attach to terrain — fighting on open ground removes his escape entirely, which is the real lane rule and appears nowhere in the full layer. Avengerang is 9s at rank 1 and damages both outbound and on the return. Dirty Fighting shields him every third hit, which eats a burst opened without a Vital ready. Riposte is 24s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Real numbers and the terrain requirement written into report[5].t, dosFull[1].d, dosFull[2].d, dontsFull[0..2].d and phases[3].why; the Grand Challenge reveal written into wants.you[1].

edits.before: Q a vital and back out — free chip he cannot answer. Identify how Akshan contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Neither side owns it — Avengerang pokes from 850 while you Lunge a Vital and step back. Trade and reset; nobody can commit yet.

edits.before: W is your matchup answer; hold it for HIS key spell only. Only take the trade when Akshan's Heroic Swing is down.
edits.after: His window: Avengerang plus a wall-attached Heroic Swing chunks you and repositions before your Lunge can connect.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Akshan must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Still his — he kite-skirmishes off terrain and pokes from brush camo faster than your chain can pin him on open ground.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Heroic Swing's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: You chain Lunges off Vital procs, he E-repositions out of each — Heroic Swing is 18s at rank 1, so trade in that gap and own the brush.

edits.before: Q-lunge the exposed vital on Akshan, AA once, and E-slow out — repeat until his bar forces the all-in he loses.
edits.after: Q-lunge the exposed vital on Akshan, AA once, and E-slow out — his Q is 9s at rank 1, so leave before it returns.

edits.before: Akshan wastes Heroic Swing — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Heroic Swing is 18s at rank 1 — once spent, run the whole pattern.

edits.before: That is Akshan's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Riposte is 24s at rank 1 — save it for his swing-in, not a stray Avengerang.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Avengerang damages going out and on the return — keep moving.

edits.before: Burning Riposte on poke — your W exists to delete his ONE key spell; waste it and the duel maths flips against you.
edits.after: Dirty Fighting shields him every third hit, so a burst opened with no Vital ready just feeds the shield and his Q trades back.

edits.before: Track Akshan's Heroic Swing: His dash + camera swing escape. Engage when it's down. When it is down — Riposte his KA, hit vitals.
edits.after: Heroic Swing (18s at rank 1) must attach to terrain — fight him on open ground and his escape has nothing to grab. Then chain Vitals.

edits.before: Reach level 6 and use Grand Challenge to clinch the all-in the moment he commits a swing or steps up to poke
edits.after: Use Grand Challenge to clinch the all-in — it reveals him, so Going Rogue camo is no escape once your ult is on

notes: The full layer's ratings for the two Skill rows are 5/10 and the two Akshan rows 4/10, keeping the 7.5/10 overall difficulty coherent with a 53.21% win rate over 327 games. Carried forward the mirror audit's caution: the page repeatedly calls Fiora's Vital damage 'percent-max-HP true damage' (whys[6], spikes[3].text, late), but Riot's Duelist's Dance text says only that hitting a Vital restores Health and grants Move Speed, and the kit flags trueDamage on Grand Challenge rather than the passive. I did not touch those strings and did not repeat the claim in anything I wrote.
